title: Stale burst-credit ledger causing hot-pool fragmentation and teardown during tenant surge
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level: Several Dedicated customers reported sudden spike in cold-starts and elevated latency during concurrent surges. Investigation showed the allocator's burst-credit ledger had stale entries that prevented hot-pool rehydration and triggered teardown logic, fragmenting capacity across nodes and causing tenant request routing to land on cold pools. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix, and follow-up engineering work.
root_cause_summary: A TTL handling bug plus leader-hand-off race left per-tenant burst-credit entries inconsistent between the autoscaler cache and the persistent allocator store. Credits aged out in the cache but were not reconciled in the store; the allocator incorrectly computed headroom and initiated pool teardown for pools it considered underutilized, causing active tenants to be isolated on cold pools when traffic spiked.
resolution_summary: Deployed a three-part fix in runtime-1.20: 1) ledger-reconciliation job that canonicalizes burst-credit state on leadership change and periodically reconciles cache vs store; 2) fixed off-by-one decrement in credit accounting during preemption paths; 3) prevented teardown for pools that show recent allocation churn within a safety window. Rolled out via canary in us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. Migration job repaired affected tenant ledgers before full rollout.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-01: Customer alert received; on-call engaged. 2026-03-02: Reproduced in staging with traffic replay; identified ledger mismatch. 2026-03-03: Patch implemented and unit tests added. 2026-03-04: Hotfix canary went to us-west-2; metrics improved for canary tenants. 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-08: Gradual regional rollout. 2026-03-09: Post-deploy checks passed; customers confirmed recovery. 2026-03-10: Marked Done and published postmortem.
comments: 2026-03-01 - 09:22 - Alert: Customer support flagged latency regression for Tenant-ACME and Tenant-Helios. Initial triage by on-call Marco Ruiz (SRE).

2026-03-01 - 13:40 - Reproduction: Traffic replay against dedicated staging cluster reproduced high cold-start rate when per-tenant bursts coincided. Allocator logs show 'credit_ttl_expired' events without store updates.
2026-03-02 - 11:05 - Root cause hypothesis: cache TTL expiration not triggering reconciliation. Added detailed logging and trace IDs for leadership handoff.
2026-03-02 - 17:12 - Engineering decision: implement reconciliation job + small accounting fix. Prioritized as P0 due to customer impact.
2026-03-03 - 02:40 - Pull request opened: runtime#5421 (ledger reconciliation + decrement fix). Added integration tests that simulate leadership change and concurrent preemption.
2026-03-04 - 07:30 - Canary deployed to us-west-2. Observed 85% reduction in cold starts for canary tenants within 30 minutes. Metrics linked in artifacts.
2026-03-05 - 18:00 - Rollout to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 started. Communication: Customer success notified impacted customers and provided mitigation steps (manual warm pools) while we rolled out fix.
2026-03-09 - 14:50 - Post-deploy: Reconciliation migration completed for 12 affected reserved pools. No regressions detected in autoscaler memory or latency.
2026-03-10 - 09:00 - Postmortem published and shared with stakeholders. Follow-up action items created.
action_items: Run ledger-reconciliation-migration for all reserved pools during next maintenance window and verify metrics
Add unit and e2e tests to cover leadership handoff + TTL expiry scenarios
Instrument a new alert: per-tenant credit-age-skew > 5m
Evaluate collapsing cache+store into single source of truth to eliminate reconciliation window
notes: Customer comms: CS drafted 'Incident resolved: Dedicated capacity cold-starts' message and sent to impacted accounts on 2026-03-04.
Trade-offs: Chose reconciliation job over immediate store-only approach to limit blast radius and keep rollback simple.
Follow-up: Consider increasing safety-window for pool-teardown when allocation churn is high; tracked in project backlog.
